title: Malaysia Holds at 38 Unhealthy Areas as Klang Valley Nears 'Very Unhealthy'; Singapore Air Improves
detail: Malaysia's nationwide haze held near its recent peak on Sept. 16, with 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recording unhealthy API readings as of 5pm, several in the Klang Valley nearing the 'very unhealthy' (201+) threshold: Johan Setia 183, Cheras 174, Shah Alam and Putrajaya/Nilai both 170, Seremban 165, Petaling Jaya 164. In Johor, Tangkak (134), Kluang (124) and Batu Pahat (103) stayed unhealthy. A further 21 areas nationwide, including stations in Sarawak and Sabah, registered moderate readings. Singapore's air quality improved for a second day after Sept. 15's historic islandwide unhealthy reading: NEA's 24-hour PSI was moderate across all regions by 11am and stood at 71-89 by 5pm (Central highest at 89), as overnight showers over Kalimantan continued to clear some haze; the agency forecast the PSI would stay in the 'moderate to low-unhealthy' range, with dry conditions persisting over Sumatra and Kalimantan and southeast/southerly winds keeping some haze risk alive.

media.caption: Haze continues to blanket the Klang Valley on Sept 16 as several stations near the 'very unhealthy' threshold

title: 'Dead Animals, Barren Fields, and Hunger': AFP Documents El Niño's Grip on Central America's Dry Corridor
detail: An AFP wire feature published Sept. 16 documented the human toll of the El Niño-driven drought across Central America's Dry Corridor, where more than 10 million people live and 80% of small-scale producers are poor, per UN figures. In San Lorenzo, Honduras, 76-year-old Lidia Ochoa said 'sometimes I break down in tears — sometimes you eat, sometimes you don't,' while farmer Francisco Molina surveyed barren fields and livestock carcasses and Darwin Cruz reported reduced dairy output after losing animals. In El Matazano, El Salvador — which recorded a scorching 42°C — 31-year-old Maria de la Paz Portillo described rationing depleted water supplies, while 53-year-old Vilma Ortiz said she had turned to growing drought-resistant chili peppers to adapt. In Cunén, Guatemala, Indigenous leader Elvira Pasa warned 'all the corn harvests are going to be lost,' with corn now selling at 50% above normal prices. WFP regional director Lena Savelli reiterated the agency's estimate that 16 million people across Latin America face El Niño-driven food shortages. The dispatch adds first-person testimony to the food-security data already tracked from Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.

media.caption: Crops drying out across Central America's Dry Corridor as El Niño-driven drought deepens
